districts.name: Accra Metropolitan
districts.rentDrivenBy: Accra Central, Jamestown, Korle Gonno, Chorkor

districts.name: Ayawaso West Wuogon Municipal
districts.rentDrivenBy: Airport Residential, Roman Ridge, Dzorwulu, East Legon

landmarks.name: Black Star Gate
landmarks.blurb: The Independence Arch at the head of Black Star Square.

landmarks.name: Independence Square
landmarks.blurb: Black Star Square. Parades, state occasions, and a great deal of open concrete.

landmarks.name: Jamestown Lighthouse
landmarks.blurb: The lighthouse over old Accra, and the best view of Ga Mashie and the fishing harbour.

landmarks.name: Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park
landmarks.blurb: Nkrumah's mausoleum and museum, on the ground where he declared independence in 1957.

landmarks.name: Osu Castle
landmarks.blurb: Christiansborg. Danish slave fort, then colonial seat, then the seat of government until 2013.

landmarks.name: Ussher Fort
landmarks.blurb: A 1649 Dutch fort in Ga Mashie, later a colonial prison.

landmarks.name: Accra Metropolitan Assembly
landmarks.blurb: The assembly for central Accra, and one of 29 in the region.

landmarks.name: Bank of Ghana
landmarks.blurb: The central bank. It regulates banks, forex bureaux and mobile money.

landmarks.name: Ghana Immigration Service
landmarks.blurb: Visas, residence permits and work permits.

landmarks.name: Jubilee House
landmarks.blurb: The seat of government and the President's office.

landmarks.name: Parliament House
landmarks.blurb: Where Ghana's 276 members of parliament sit.

landmarks.name: Supreme Court of Ghana
landmarks.blurb: The apex court, and the seat of the Judicial Service.

landmarks.name: Artists Alliance Gallery
landmarks.blurb: Three floors of Ghanaian art on the Labadi shore.

landmarks.name: Arts Centre
landmarks.blurb: Crafts, textiles and hard bargaining, near Independence Square.

landmarks.name: National Museum of Ghana
landmarks.blurb: Archaeology, ethnography and art, in a listed 1957 rotunda.

landmarks.name: National Theatre
landmarks.blurb: The sail-shaped 1992 theatre, home to the national dance, drama and symphony companies.

landmarks.name: Nubuke Foundation
landmarks.blurb: Contemporary Ghanaian art, in East Legon.

landmarks.name: Accra Mall
landmarks.blurb: The first modern mall in Ghana, at the Tetteh Quarshie interchange.

landmarks.name: Agbogbloshie
landmarks.blurb: Scrap, electronics and the Konkomba yam market.

landmarks.name: Kaneshie Market
landmarks.blurb: A vast covered market west of the centre, strongest on food.

landmarks.name: Kantamanto Market
landmarks.blurb: One of the world's largest second-hand clothing markets.

landmarks.name: Madina Market
landmarks.blurb: The market for the northern suburbs, busiest at the weekend.

landmarks.name: Makola Market
landmarks.blurb: Central Accra's market. If it is sold in Ghana, it is sold here.

landmarks.name: West Hills Mall
landmarks.blurb: The largest mall in the country, out at Weija.

landmarks.name: Achimota Terminal
landmarks.blurb: A major northern transport hub and market.

landmarks.name: Kotoka International Airport
landmarks.blurb: Ghana's main airport, and about twenty minutes from most of Accra outside rush hour.

landmarks.name: Kwame Nkrumah Circle
landmarks.blurb: Circle. The interchange, the lorry station and the electronics market all at once.

landmarks.name: Port of Tema
landmarks.blurb: Ghana's main port. Almost everything imported arrives here.

landmarks.name: Tema Station
landmarks.blurb: A central trotro terminal, despite the name being in Accra.

landmarks.name: Accra Technical University
landmarks.blurb: Technical and vocational higher education in the centre of town.

landmarks.name: Achimota School
landmarks.blurb: Founded 1927, and one of the most consequential schools in West Africa.

landmarks.name: GIMPA
landmarks.blurb: Public administration, law and business, at Achimota.

landmarks.name: UPSA
landmarks.blurb: The University of Professional Studies, strong on accountancy and business.

landmarks.name: University of Ghana, Legon
landmarks.blurb: Ghana's oldest and largest university, founded 1948.

landmarks.name: 37 Military Hospital
landmarks.blurb: Military hospital that treats civilians, and a major trauma centre.

landmarks.name: Korle Bu Teaching Hospital
landmarks.blurb: Ghana's largest hospital and its main teaching hospital, founded 1923.

landmarks.name: Ridge Hospital
landmarks.blurb: The Greater Accra Regional Hospital, rebuilt and expanded in 2017.

landmarks.name: UG Medical Centre
landmarks.blurb: A newer teaching hospital on the Legon campus.

landmarks.name: Achimota Forest
landmarks.blurb: A protected forest reserve inside the city, and a long-running political argument.

landmarks.name: Ada Foah
landmarks.blurb: Where the Volta meets the sea, at the eastern edge of the region.

landmarks.name: Bojo Beach
landmarks.blurb: Reached by a short boat across the lagoon, which is half the appeal.

landmarks.name: Kokrobite Beach
landmarks.blurb: An hour west, and the closest thing Accra has to a beach village.

landmarks.name: Labadi Beach
landmarks.blurb: La Pleasure Beach. Busiest on Sundays and public holidays.

landmarks.name: Sakumono Ramsar Site
landmarks.blurb: A protected coastal wetland between Accra and Tema, and important for birds.

landmarks.name: Shai Hills Reserve
landmarks.blurb: Baboons, antelope and caves, an hour up the Akosombo road and still in the region.

meta.source: Ghana Statistical Service, 2021 Population and Housing Census
meta.note: Real census counts at district level. The 2021 census uses the post-2018 districts, so these join to the 29 Greater Accra assemblies directly. Percentages are computed here from the counts; the counts are as published.

meta.basis: Indicative ranking of typical asking rents, from listing observation and local knowledge. Not a survey, and not published data - Ghana has none at this level.

bands.label: Lowest
bands.note: Rural and semi-rural. Far below the city median, and far from work.

bands.label: Below median
bands.note: Dense older neighbourhoods and the outer commuter belt.

bands.label: Around the median
bands.note: The bulk of ordinary Accra housing.

bands.label: Above median
bands.note: Established suburbs with newer stock and shorter commutes.

bands.label: Highest
bands.note: Diplomatic and executive Accra. Often quoted in dollars.

meta.what: Inputs for the map's modelled noise layers. Not measured noise and not decibels - nobody publishes ambient noise by district for Accra.
sources: Roads and premises: OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL
Population: Ghana Statistical Service, 2021 Population and Housing Census
District boundaries and areas: geoBoundaries (gbOpen), CC BY 4.0
meta.method: Road length and premises counted within each district and divided by its area. Roads are attributed to the district containing their midpoint. The combined layer averages the three quintile ranks with equal weight, which introduces no coefficients.
